messages:
jane_cust: Hey team - our dedicated pool for tenant acme-inc started returning a lot of 429s around 10:04 UTC and latency spiked to 1.2s. Customer is seeing failed batches in production, can someone look?

alex_support: Sorry to hear that, can you paste an example request/response (headers) and which model/route?

jane_cust: Curl snippet: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"rw-medium-1","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-tenant-rate-limit: 12
x-rw-tenant-quota: 12/60s
Retry-After: 5
```

jane_cust: We used to see x-rw-tenant-rate-limit: 120. Nothing in our code changed.

samir_eng: I'm pulling dedicated pool metrics. On the host pool we have a sudden drop in allowed RPS for tenant acme-inc at 10:03 UTC. Autoscale looks fine, GPU utilization normal.

ops_ana: I see the same in the tenant quota service logs: at 10:02 a configuration push from infra-configs updated tenant acme-inc quota to 12 (units/sec) instead of 120. Likely a units mismatch from a YAML entry (per-second vs per-minute).

maria_oncall: Did the config push come from a deploy or a manual edit? Any CI run id?

ops_ana: It was from a bulk apply script: infra-configs CI #4827. The change payload had "rate_limit: 12" and the parser treated it as 'per-second' for dedicated, whereas previously we stored per-minute in legacy entries. So a conversion bug bit us.

alex_support: Can we hotfix to restore previous quota? Customer needs immediate mitigation.

samir_eng: Two mitigation paths: 1) Roll back the CI commit that applied new values (fast, but needs approvals and may affect other tenants). 2) Patch tenant-quota service to treat legacy numeric values as per-minute when needed and apply conversion to per-second (non-disruptive for other pools). For immediate relief we can override acme-inc with a temporary tenant-specific override via admin API.

maria_oncall: Create override + notify customer. Also enable autoscale burst to allow queued requests through while we roll fix. I can run the admin override now if someone approves.

alex_support: Approve. Please set to 120 rps and bump burst to 200 for 10 minutes.

samir_eng: Doing admin override: 
```bash
# admin CLI
redwood-admin tenant override-acme --rate-limit 120 --burst 200 --ttl 600
Response: OK override applied, id=ovr-9832
```

samir_eng: Override applied at 10:12 UTC. Monitoring shows 429 rate dropping immediately and latency returning to ~90ms for successful requests.

jane_cust: Confirmed - 429s stopped after 10:13, thanks! But can you confirm root cause and next steps so we don't hit this again?

ops_ana: Root cause: config parser mismatch between new CI schema (per-second) and legacy config values (per-minute). A queued conversion routine didn't run for legacy entries during the recent config migration. The CI applied values unintentionally low.

maria_oncall: Postmortem action items: 1) Patch parser to validate units and reject ambiguous values with CI guard. 2) Add a canary that validates quota deltas >5x for a single tenant and auto-opens an alert. 3) Add an automated remediation to detect sudden tenant quota drops and apply temporary override. 4) Customer notification template.

alex_support: I'll own the customer comms and escalate billing/credits if needed.

samir_eng: I'll open a PR to patch parser and add unit tests for legacy config conversions. Link: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/7591 (WIP).

ops_ana: Also found a noisy-neighbor risk: the quota service exposed per-tenant rate limits to the routing layer and the routing layer did not revalidate after override because of a cache TTL of 5m. We should invalidate routing cache on overrides.

maria_oncall: Good catch. Add cache invalidation to action items.

samir_eng: Repro steps documented for runbook: 
1) Simulate config push with legacy per-minute value for tenant -> apply to staging dedicated pool.
2) Observe quota service metric `tenant_allowance_rps` drop and routing `429` spike.
3) Use admin CLI to set override and confirm routing cache invalidate and traffic recovery.

I added a short runbook entry in the ops-runbooks repo.

jane_cust: Appreciate the quick response. We'll keep an eye but please let us know when the parser patch is live.

alex_support: Will update when PR merges and when parser fix is deployed. Also scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 16:00 UTC.

maria_oncall: Postmortem agenda: timeline, root cause, remediation plan, and confirmation of routing cache invalidation.

ops_ana: Follow-up: running a scan for other tenants with suspiciously low quotas now. Found 3 more tenants with values off by factor of 10, creating tickets to notify their account managers.

samir_eng: Thanks team. I'll push a hotfix to make the parser strict and add a CI lint to block ambiguous units. Target release in 24h.

alex_support: Marking this thread resolved for now. Will reopen if customer reports recurrence. :white_check_mark:
